market_question: Will Renan Santos finish in second place in the first round of the 2026 Brazilian presidential election?
reasoning: Renan Santos is a fringe candidate with no significant polling support or major party backing, making a second-place finish in the first round astronomically unlikely. Historical patterns in Brazilian presidential elections show that second place goes to a well-known national figure, not an obscure activist. The market's 5.9% implied probability is at least 50× too high.
evidence_points: No credible polls or media reports mention Renan Santos as a top-tier contender for 2026.
In the 2022 election, the second spot was taken by Jair Bolsonaro with 43.2% of valid votes; minor candidates like Léo Péricles or Sofia Manzano received <0.1%.
Even if the field fractures, the second-place candidate typically needs >15%–20% support, which Renan Santos has never approached.
sources_consulted: News monitoring for 2026 candidate announcements (no mention of Renan Santos as a serious contender)
